title: BTTackler: A Diagnosis-based Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Hyperparameter Optimization

problem.claim: Deep learning hyperparameter optimization is costly, and bad trials can consume substantial computation resources.

gap.claim: Accuracy-based automated HPO methods may fail to reflect severe training problems during early training, leading to inefficient optimization trajectories.

contributions.claim: BTTackler is an HPO framework that uses training diagnosis to automatically identify and tackle bad trials.
BTTackler calculates quantified training indicators for each trial and triggers early termination when training problems are detected.
The paper proposes two measurements based on accuracy and time consumption to quantify the effectiveness of automated HPO methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe BTTackler as a novel HPO framework that introduces training diagnosis for automatically identifying training problems and tackling bad trials.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations cover HPO tasks using three classical deep neural networks and four widely used HPO methods.
On average, BTTackler reduces time consumption by 40.33% to achieve the same accuracy comparable to baseline methods.
Within a given time budget, BTTackler conducts 44.5% more top-10 trials than baseline methods on average.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning HPO is costly, and automated approaches commonly guide trials using accuracy metrics.
Training problems may be invisible to early accuracy metrics, causing bad trials to consume resources and reduce optimization efficiency.
BTTackler diagnoses trials with quantified indicators and terminates trials early when problems are detected.
The framework is evaluated across representative tasks, neural networks, and HPO methods, using proposed accuracy- and time-based measurements.
The authors report reduced time consumption, more top-10 trials within a time budget, and an open-source Python library for applying the framework.

source_observation.claim: Early accuracy metrics may not reveal severe training problems such as vanishing gradients or insufficient convergence.

interpretation.claim: Optimization systems may benefit from monitoring diagnostic signals in addition to the primary performance metric.

application.claim: For resource-constrained automated search, detect and terminate clearly failing trials early when reliable diagnostic indicators are available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which diagnostic indicators generalize across models, tasks, or training regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the quantified indicators used for diagnosis.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated datasets, neural network architectures, baseline methods, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide variance, statistical testing, or detailed comparison results.
The abstract does not describe the two proposed measurements formally.
The abstract does not specify the library version, license, or implementation details.
